parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish آغا (ağa) (compare Turkish ağa) or Greek άγιος (ágios).

parole.significato: coarse rug, blanket, carpet, traditionally of goat's hair
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish چرگه (çerge), with the c- form via Greek τσέργα (tsérga).
From Ottoman Turkish قلمار (Turkish kalamar (“squid”)), from Greek καλαμάρι (kalamári).

parole.significato: kallikantzaros: goblin with magic powers and wearing a chain mail shirt
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قره قونجلوس (kara koncolos, “black bogey, black werewolf”); Kosovar Gheg Albanian kallukanxhë is from Greek καλλικάντσαρος (kallikántsaros), also from Turkish.

parole.significato: A kind of fabric, usually coloured, used for women's clothing.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish لاهوری (lâhuri). The masculine was likely mediated by Greek λαχούρι (lachoúri).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish پانایر (panayir), from Greek πανηγύρι (panigýri, “gathering of people”) from Ancient Greek πανήγυρις (panḗguris, “high festival”).

parole.significato: orange, sweet orange (Citrus × aurantium var. sinensis)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish پورتقال (portokal), with /l/ forms from Greek πορτοκάλι (portokáli).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish راهوان (rahvan, “ambling pace”) in its Gheg forms. The originally Tosk form revan is probably via Greek ρεβάνι (reváni).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish سونگر (sünger), from Greek σφουγγάρι (sfoungári). Doublet of shpuzë and shponxë.
